objective: Compute exactly, as reduced rational functions over GF(2), the 2(n - 1) entries of the corner's row of K_n^-1 (the walk series from c to the v contacts (0, 2b + 1) and (N, 2b + 1)) at the training sides n = 4, 8, 16, 32; look for one uniform rule giving every entry at every n = 2^m, in the frozen alphabet; commit it before the exact row at side 64 is computed; then test it at 64. Verdict: closed form, partial rule, or no pattern, as frozen.
status: Closed 2026-11-11 (pre-registered in c53bb2861; the training verdict and the predictions committed in 128b2e30d before side 64; refereed): a partial rule only, so no closed form. Rules in the frozen alphabet hold for the six entries next to the corners, all known or derivable before registration (the corner return law, the four-corner formula and two relations of the powers of two); none was found for the other 2(n - 1) - 6 entries. 128b2e30d's 'no pattern' is corrected to this (docs/CORRECTIONS.md, 2026-11-11). Proved: the corner row of K_n^-1 is the walk series from the corner to the v contacts of the two side walls. Computed exactly at 4 to 64, side 64 held out: the denominators' factors are exactly the minimal polynomials of the classes a in GF(2n)* with Kloosterman sum K(a) != 0, every such class appearing (that only these occur follows from the spectrum); every denominator is a perfect square; the largest exponent is 2 ceil(|K(a)|/8), not the spectrum's |K(a)|/2; along each wall the entries have the generic linear complexity n/2 (certified exactly).
title: The corner's row: exact rows, a frozen rule, a held-out test
